slides.headline: The Pentagon Backs More Launch Capacity
slides.subheadline: Conditional loans target two SpaceX competitors as military launch requirements grow.

points.title: Stoke Space
points.body: Additional launch infrastructure for Nova Block 2.

points.title: Rocket Lab
points.body: Production, recovery, and processing upgrades for Neutron.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use the publication palette throughout all slides. Below the headline, split one abstract capital-flow line into two rising trajectories, terminating at the two company labels. Use dashed accent paths to indicate conditional commitments, not completed transfers. Keep both callouts outside the trajectories; avoid literal rocket silhouettes or implied orbital specifications.

slides.headline: Equal Loans, Different Capacity Targets
slides.subheadline: OSC backs a second launch pad and efforts to increase Neutron’s flight rate.

comparison.body: Second launch pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida.
Increase Neutron’s flight rate through production, recovery, and processing upgrades.

slides.svgBlueprint: Create two equal-width ledger columns separated by a thin vertical rule. Set each exact loan amount prominently above its purpose. Beneath Stoke, draw an abstract launch-pad platform; beneath Rocket Lab, draw a circular processing arrow. Give both columns dashed borders labeled conditional. Equal geometry represents equal commitments, not equal readiness.

slides.headline: The Requirement Has More Than Doubled
slides.subheadline: Space Systems Command forecasts up to 249 military medium-to-heavy-lift launches.

points.title: up to 249
points.body: Forecast military medium-to-heavy-lift launches through the early 2030s.

points.title: more than double
points.body: Compared with Space Systems Command’s expectation just two years ago.

slides.svgBlueprint: Place the exact phrase up to above an oversized 249 occupying the upper diagram field. Underline it with a broad accent rule. Put the comparison statement in a narrow bottom ribbon connected by an upward arrow. Do not draw proportional bars, invent a baseline count, or convert the forecast into an annual rate.

slides.headline: An Ordering Cutoff, Not Immediate Retirement
slides.subheadline: Commercial restrictions and military contract windows describe different milestones.

milestones.title: Commercial Falcon 9
milestones.body: SpaceX has stopped taking commercial orders for launches after 2028.

milestones.title: Military ordering
milestones.body: Space Force can order Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy missions.

milestones.title: Military launches
milestones.body: Actual launches under the Space Force contract can extend through 2033.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw three vertically separated horizontal timeline lanes with exact date phrases at their endpoints. Differentiate commercial orders, military orders, and military launches using line patterns. Use schematic rather than proportional spacing. Never add a Falcon retirement marker; the dossier supplies no fixed retirement date.

slides.headline: Assured Access Needs Multiple Working Rockets
slides.subheadline: Vulcan’s groundings pushed several national security missions to SpaceX.

points.title: at least two
points.body: US rocket programs supported under assured-access policy since the 1990s.

points.title: twice in the last two years
points.body: Solid rocket booster problems grounded Vulcan.

slides.svgBlueprint: Build an abstract network with a national-security payload node above two schematic launch routes. Label the diagram policy schematic so route count is not mistaken for an inventory. Place an interruption symbol on a separate Vulcan annotation and redirect its dashed mission arrow toward SpaceX. Anchor the two factual callouts on opposite margins.

slides.headline: Do Not Confuse The Nova Milestones
slides.subheadline: The loan supports Block 2 infrastructure; the stated debut timing concerns Pathfinder.

comparison.body: Described as fully reusable; debut set for sometime next year.
Upgraded Pathfinder; planned second launch site supports flights. No debut date stated.

slides.svgBlueprint: Arrange two labeled vehicle-name bands diagonally as a development lineage, linked by an arrow labeled upgraded version. Use abstract capsule outlines, not technical vehicle drawings. Attach the relative debut phrase only to Pathfinder and a launch-pad icon only to Block 2. Do not translate next year into a calendar year.

slides.headline: The Loan Targets The Turnaround
slides.subheadline: Neutron is medium-class and partially reusable; proposed funding targets its operational support infrastructure.

points.title: Delivery and processing
points.body: Support faster vehicle delivery and processing.

points.title: Recovery and transport
points.body: Expand maritime vessels and equipment for Neutron recovery and transport.

points.title: Production and turnaround
points.body: Increase composite-structure and engine production; add infrastructure to reduce launch turnaround.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw a triangular process loop with exactly three broad nodes: processing, maritime recovery, and manufacturing. Use abstract handling, vessel, and engine icons. Connect nodes with dashed accent arrows indicating intended operational improvements. Keep all explanatory text outside the loop; show no invented throughput, turnaround duration, or completed operational cycle.

slides.headline: A Higher Price Before Flight
slides.subheadline: Rocket Lab attributes the increase to surging bookings for the still-unproven vehicle.
slides.svgBlueprint: Create a single ascending price bridge: place the previous amount at lower left and the new amount at upper right, joined by an accent step. Treat positions as editorial hierarchy rather than a quantitative axis. Keep exact price strings visible; do not add a calculated percentage, margin, or revenue projection.

slides.headline: The Backlog Is Not Neutron Alone
slides.subheadline: Rocket Lab’s combined orders and Neutron’s scheduled debut describe different things.

points.title: 117 launches
points.body: Contracted backlog combines Neutron and Electron orders; no split is provided.

points.title: next year
points.body: Rocket Lab’s stated Neutron first-launch schedule, not a completed milestone.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw one undivided backlog container labeled 117 launches, with Neutron and Electron named beneath a shared brace. Do not segment the container or imply either vehicle’s share. Below it, place a separate dashed launch milestone labeled next year, disconnected from backlog quantities. Maintain a wide visual gap between orders and readiness.

slides.headline: Capital Support Is Not Launch Readiness
slides.subheadline: Both loans remain conditional; the article does not establish completed disbursement.

points.title: Funding conditions
points.body: Financial, legal, technical, investment, due diligence, and other requirements apply.

points.title: Flight milestones
points.body: Pathfinder and Neutron debuts remain scheduled; Block 2 has no stated date.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use a full-height editorial gate: a dashed capital arrow approaches a narrow vertical threshold labeled conditional. Place funding requirements above the threshold and flight milestones below it as two distinct annotations. Stop the arrow before an abstract launch horizon. Do not depict funds as disbursed or vehicles as operational.
